title: The Biggest Chimp Group Ever Known Split in Two. Then the Killing Began

scenes.text: The largest chimpanzee group ever known tore itself in two.
At Ngogo, in Uganda, scientists have followed one community since 1995. It grew to between 150 and 200 chimpanzees.
Around 2015 it began to pull apart. By 2018 it was two groups, Western and Central, that no longer mixed.
Then the Western chimps began raiding. By 2024 they had killed at least seven adult males and seventeen infants from the other side.
These weren't strangers. The victims had fed, groomed and patrolled beside their attackers for years.
Humans have seen this only once before, at Gombe in the 1970s. There, one side killed every male of the other.

description:
The Ngogo chimpanzees of Kibale National Park, Uganda, were the largest wild chimpanzee community known, with roughly 150 to 200 members. After growing polarisation from 2015 they split permanently into Western and Central groups by 2018.
Between 2018 and 2024 the Western group killed at least seven adult males and seventeen infants of the Central group, animals they had lived, fed and groomed with for years. The study, built on three decades of observation, was published in Science in April 2026. The only earlier case was the Gombe conflict of 1974 to 1978.
Does this change how you see chimpanzees?
subject: chimpanzee group
first_comment: The lead author warns against calling it a civil war: it's a group split followed by lethal attacks. Did you know chimps did this?
